g.text: Match rigor to consequences and dependencies
Failure consequences, replacement cost, dependencies and maintenance burden define the decision.

A one-use helper can become a shared process with downstream dependents. Revisit who relies on it, which failures matter and how recovery works. Isolation and limited scope can reduce exposure, but a label such as prototype or temporary is not an enforcing control.
Invest in the cheap safe path

Provide standard choices, test fixtures/fakes and quick low-noise feedback. Make it easier to create a complete working slice with checks than to postpone them. Shared verification infrastructure compounds across tasks and allows practitioners to focus on the remaining judgment.
Apply the same standard to artifacts

For a report or presentation, acceptance includes the current saved output, its evidence and readability. For a financial action, it includes authorization and recovery. Match the check to the actual consequence; neither code generation speed nor another agent’s confidence resolves that decision.
Sources: Capital One · Sonar | Reviewed October 25, 2026
